title: In Situ SEM-EBSD Tensile Study of GH4169 Alloy with Different Grain Sizes
publisher: MDPI (span: "Licensee MDPI, Basel, Switzerland." pdftotext line 42)

license.span: This article is an open access article distributed under the terms and conditions of the Creative Commons Attribution (CC BY) license.

materials_domain: Ni-based superalloy GH4169 (Inconel 718); grain-size effect on in situ tensile deformation

sample_series.varied: grain size via heat treatment (980 °C vs 1050 °C, 1 h, water quench); in situ displacement ΔL on each specimen

conditions.label: fine-grained (heat treatment A)
conditions.value: 980 °C/1 h + WQ; average grain size 10.7 µm

conditions.label: coarse-grained (heat treatment B)
conditions.value: 1050 °C/1 h + WQ; average grain size 70.6 µm

other_series: in situ displacement on the same specimen: EBSD at ΔL = 0, 600, 900 µm (3 states; IPF/IPF-texture also at yield); SEM at ΔL = 0, elastic, yield, 600, 900, 1800 µm (fine) and 0, yield, 600, 900, 1800, 2200 µm (coarse)
sample_series.notes: Only two material conditions; the ≥3-condition series is a strain (displacement) series within one in situ test per specimen. One specimen per grain size (no replicates stated).
spans: specimens with average grain sizes of 10.7 µm and 70.6 µm were fabricated via different heat treatment processes

Heat treatment process A: Heated uniformly to 980 °C at a heating rate of 30 °C/min, held at the predetermined temperature for 1 h, and then immediately cooled by water quenching. Heat treatment process B: Heated uniformly to 1050 °C
electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD) data were synchronously collected when the displacement was 0 µm, 600 µm and 900 µm, respectively.

methods_measured.quantity: in situ surface morphology during tension
methods_measured.instrument: Tescan 8000 SEM with in situ tensile stage
methods_measured.span: The in situ tensile tests were carried out at room temperature using an in situ tensile stage compatible with a scanning electron microscope (Tescan 8000, produced by TESCAN GROUP, a. s., Brno, Czech Republic) chamber

methods_measured.instrument: EBSD in the SEM (detector not named); AZtecCrystal 2.1 processing
methods_measured.span: The raw EBSD data collected above were systematically processed and analyzed using AZtecCrystal 2.1.

The SEM accelerating voltage was set to 20 kV. the electron beam current was 1 nA, and the working distance was 20 mm. The EBSD mapping area for the fine-grained specimen is 175 × 130 µm, while that for the coarsegrained specimen is 600 × 450 µm.

methods_measured.instrument: in situ tensile stage, built-in grating ruler
methods_measured.span: The displacement is measured by the built-in grating ruler of the in situ system, which represents the total deformation of the specimen excluding the gauge section.
EDS mapping was performed on fine-grained and coarse-grained specimens.

computed_quantities.quantity: grain size (ECD) distribution and mean (10.7 / 70.6 µm)
computed_quantities.method: EBSD grain reconstruction, equivalent circle diameter, histogram
computed_quantities.span: The equivalent circle diameter (ECD) was used to characterize the grain size. The statistical results of the grain size for the two specimens are shown in Figure 2c,d.
a threshold angle of 5° was applied for KAM calculation [37]. The neighborhood order of KAM is set to the first order.

the texture intensity of the fine-grained specimen slowly increases from the initial value of 1.17 to 1.51 and remains at a relatively low level. In contrast, the texture intensity of coarse-grained specimens increases sharply from 1.10 to 2.68

computed_quantities.quantity: Schmid factors of slip systems (Tables 1, 2; F11 maps)
computed_quantities.span: The Mtex 5.11.1 toolbox in MATLAB 2019 was used to analyze the typical grains of both specimens.
The grain boundary densities of the two specimens were calculated. The fine-grained specimen has a grain boundary density of 0.3027, while that of the coarse-grained specimen is 0.0466.

mechanisms.mechanism: grain size limits dislocation slip length; fine grains distribute deformation uniformly
mechanisms.span: In situ SEM results reveal that the grain size directly determines the maximum slip length of dislocations.

mechanisms.mechanism: grain boundaries act as strain barriers dispersing local stress (fine grains)
mechanisms.span: Grain boundaries act as “strain barriers”, which effectively disperse local stress and inhibit strain concentration

mechanisms.mechanism: preferential activation of high-Schmid-factor slip systems causing intragranular inhomogeneity
mechanisms.span: slip systems with high Schmid factors are preferentially activated in both fine and coarse grains, resulting in inhomogeneous intragranular deformation and concentrated slip bands.

mechanisms.mechanism: weak grain-boundary constraint in coarse grains → long-range preferential rotation and [111] texture
mechanisms.span: coarse grains have insufficient grain boundary constraints, deformation is dominated by a few dominant slip systems, and grains undergo unconstrained long-range preferential rotation.

mechanisms.mechanism: grain-boundary sliding as auxiliary mechanism at large strain (fine grains)
mechanisms.span: suggesting that grain-boundary sliding has become an auxiliary deformation mechanism, which cooperates with intragranular slip to accommodate plastic deformation

mechanisms.mechanism: correlation between grain size and grain Schmid factor
mechanisms.span: It can be seen that there is no clear correlation between grain size and the Schmid factor of individual grains.
SEM observations indicate that no δ-phase precipitation is detected in the two specimens

summary: GH4169 superalloy at two grain sizes (10.7 vs 70.6 µm, two heat treatments) tested in situ in a Tescan SEM with EBSD at ΔL = 0/600/900 µm. Rich scale-barred micrographs and EBSD maps, but only 2 material conditions and few plots (1 line, 1 bar, 4 histograms). CC BY (MDPI).
